title: Mean vs median (salaries)
examples: When should I use the median instead of the mean for salary data?
What does it mean if salary data is positively skewed?
Can you explain how outliers affect the mean?

explain.say: Today we are comparing the mean and the median for salaries. These are both ways to find an average value. We must choose the right one for the job market.
The mean is calculated by summing all salaries and dividing by the number of people. It uses every single data point in its calculation. This gives a mathematical center point.
The median is simply the middle value when all salaries are arranged in order. If there is an even number of salaries, you find the average of the two middle numbers. This represents the true center.
Skew describes the shape of your salary data distribution. If the tail points right, we call it positively skewed. This often happens with high earners.
When data is highly skewed by a few very high salaries, the mean is pulled upwards. The median remains a more accurate representation of the typical salary. You should report the median.
In a company salary survey, the mean might suggest high pay, but the median tells you what most employees actually earn. Always check for skewness first.

faq.q: If the data is perfectly symmetrical, is the mean equal to the median?
faq.a: Yes, in a perfectly symmetrical distribution, the mean and the median will be equal. This means the average accurately reflects the center point.
asks: Are mean and median the same if the data is normal?

faq.q: Should I always report the median salary to avoid bias?
faq.a: No, you should only use the median if the data is significantly skewed by extreme values. If the data is normal, the mean is also appropriate.
asks: Is median always safer than mean?
When is it okay to use the mean?

faq.q: What is an outlier in the context of salary data?
faq.a: An outlier is an unusually high or low salary compared to the rest of the group. These extreme values can pull the mean away from the typical salary.
asks: What causes skew in salary data?
How do outliers affect the average?

faq.q: Can I calculate the mean manually if I have a small dataset?
faq.a: Yes, you can manually sum all the values and then divide by the total count. This helps build understanding before using software.
asks: How do I calculate the mean by hand?
What is the first step for finding the mean?

faq.q: If I have two different groups, which average should I use for comparison?
faq.a: You must check the skewness of both groups separately. Comparing the medians is often the safest approach unless both are symmetrical.
asks: How do I compare two sets of data averages?

facts: The median is the value that splits the data into two equal halves.
Positive skew means the tail of the data extends towards higher values.
When data is skewed, the mean is more sensitive to outliers than the median.
A normal distribution is symmetrical, meaning mean equals median.

quiz.say: A small tech startup reports salaries: 30k, 35k, 40k, 45k, and 1,000k. Which measure is best?
quiz.why: The median is best because the 1,000k salary is an outlier that drastically pulls the mean upwards.

wrong.0: You might choose the mean because it uses every single number in the calculation.
wrong.1: You might choose the mode because it is also a measure of central tendency.
wrong.2: You might choose the range because it shows the full spread of the data.

quiz.say: If the salary data is perfectly symmetrical, what relationship exists between the mean and median?
quiz.why: Symmetrical data means the average value is perfectly balanced, so the mean and median will be the same.

wrong.1: This is only true if the data is negatively skewed.
wrong.2: This is only true if the data is positively skewed.
wrong.3: Both are valid measures when the data is balanced.

quiz.say: A dataset has values: 10, 12, 15, 18, 20. What is the median?
quiz.why: The median is the middle number when the data is ordered, which is 15.

wrong.0: You might average the two middle numbers incorrectly.
wrong.1: You might choose the second number instead of the actual middle value.
wrong.3: You might average the two middle numbers, but there is only one middle number here.
